newsitem.title: USA: Merrill gets new neighbor atop the hill.
newsitem.headline: Merrill gets new neighbor atop the hill.

text.p: After decades alone at the top of the heap, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc finally has a fight on its hands.

As Wall Street stares at a brokerage landscape suddenly twin-towered by the merger of Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter, Discover & Co, many wonder what response will come from the former undisputed champ.
Viewed in the most basic terms, Morgan Stanley's deal renders complex what had been the simplest question on Wall Street: Who's the biggest?
"Now I'd say, 'How are you measuring that?'," said Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette analyst Joan Solotar. "I think I'd go with Morgan Stanley-Dean Witter."
Officially, Merrill has shrugged off the merger announcement, focusing instead on the fact that the firm's success drove competitors such as Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter to emulate it.
"A merger of this sort comes as no surprise," a Merrill spokesman said. "This merger confirms the validity of our own business strategy."
While analysts agreed that Merrill faces little immediate threat from the combination, few bought the business-as-usual attitude.
"They'd like you to believe they didn't notice the deal," said Perrin Long, an independent analyst who covers the securities industry. "But they noticed it."
Merrill still has a slew of statistics to support its claim to the number one spot.
Merrill's revenues would still comfortably outpace those of the combined company, and its 14,000-strong army of retail brokers far outstrips those of its competitors.
Analysts said it would take some time before anyone could judge whether the Morgan Stanley-Dean Witter combination represented a threat to topple Merrill as overall leader.
But what has vanished is the idea that Merrill stands alone as the one firm that could do it all.
"What the acquisition does is take away some of the uniqueness of the Merrill franchise," Solotar said. "But Merrill still has a top-quality distribution system that at this point remains unmatched."
If the merger goes smoothly -- a huge if, because many major mergers on Wall Street have flopped -- an interesting race lies ahead.
"Merrill really hasn't been tested like this," Long said. "This could be like watching Secretariat running a race against War Admiral."
